Accidental release prevention and emergency response policies:

Sawtooth Caverns has implemented all the elements of an EPA 40 CFR Part 68 Accidental Release Prevention Requirements, Program 3 Risk Management Plan (RMP) and all the elements of OSHA 29 CFR Part 1910.119 Process Safety Management (PSM) of Highly Hazardous Chemicals regulation.  Sawtooth Caverns complies with National Fire Protection Association NFPA-58 Liquefied Petroleum Gas Code requirements for LP-Gas Storage, and it is company policy to adhere to all applicable federal, state, and local laws.  If an emergency were to occur, it is company policy to notify the Millard County Sheriff's Department and request that they respond to the emergency.

Sawtooth Caverns also operates a refined fuel products storage facility, where non-RMP-regulated fuels are stored and distributed by rail and transport truck. The facility complies with the National Fire Protection Associations NFPA 30  Flammable Liquids Code. In the event of an emergency, company policy is to immediately notify the Millard County Sheriffs Department and request their response.

The Stationary Source and Regulated substances:

Sawtooth Caverns is a bulk liquefied petroleum gas storage facility that receives propane and butane by rail car and customer truck transports.  Propane and butane are stored at Sawtooth Caverns and distributed by railcar or customer truck transports.

General Accidental Release Prevention Program:
Sawtooth Caverns has developed and implemented all the elements of the EPA 40 CFR Part 68 Accidental Release Prevention Requirements, Program 3 Risk Management Plan (RMP) and all the elements of OSHA 29 CFR Part 1910.119 Process Safety Management (PSM) of Highly Hazardous Chemicals regulations.  Sawtooth NGL Caverns adheres to the National Fire Protection Association NFPA-58 Liquefied Petroleum Gas Code requirements for LP-Gas Storage and all applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Process Safety Information (PSI):  Saw

tooth Caverns has compiled written process safety information for all PSM covered processes.  The process safety information includes the hazards of chemicals used or produced in the process, process technology information, and process equipment data.  The process safety information is updated whenever process changes are made using management of changes and pre-startup safety reviews.
Accurate and complete process safety information enables Sawtooth Caverns employees involved in operating and maintaining the terminal to identify and understand the hazards of the process.  Process safety information is used to conduct process hazard analysis on the existing process or a proposed modification to a process.

Process Hazard Analysis (PHA):  Sawtooth Caverns is committed to performing a detailed hazard analysis of each covered process to identify, evaluate, and control hazards involved in the processes.  Each process is systematically examined to identify potential hazards, controls in place to manage these hazards, and recommend additional controls, as appropriate.
Sawtooth NGL Caverns uses the hazard and operability (HAZOP) and check list PHA methodologies, which are conducted by a team of people who have operating and maintenance experience, engineering expertise and PHA facilitator training.  The PHA team identifies and evaluates potential hazards of the process as well as accident prevention and mitigation measures, and makes suggestions for additional prevention and / or mitigation measures.
As a minimum Sawtooth Caverns performs periodic PHA reviews or revalidations every 5 years as long as the process is operating.
PHA findings and recommendations and their resolution are documented.  Sawtooth Caverns has implemented a system to address and resolve all PHA findings and recommendations in a timely manner through a written schedule.  All PHA findings and recommendation resolutions are communicated to all effected employees.  All recommendations must be resolved an

d documented by management.

Operating Procedures (OP):  Sawtooth Caverns has developed and implemented written operating procedures that describe the tasks that terminal operators and transport drivers must perform, the safe process operating parameters that must be maintained, and safety precautions for operations and maintenance activities.  Sawtooth NGL Caverns written operating procedures address steps for each operating phase, including: (1) initial start-up, (2) normal operations, (3) temporary operations, (4) emergency shutdown, (5) emergency operations, (6) normal shutdown, and (7) start-up after turnaround.  
Sawtooth Caverns written operating procedures state the operating limits including the consequences of deviation and the steps required to correct or avoid the deviation.  Sawtooth Caverns written operating procedures describe all the process safety systems and their functions.
Sawtooth Caverns written operating procedures are reviewed and certified annually for current practices and accuracy.

Safe Work Practices and Procedures:  Sawtooth Caverns has developed and implemented safe work practices in accordance with the OSHA 29 CFR Part 1910 requirements that include methods for controlling plant entry, presence and exit of support personnel, and lockout/ tagout procedures to ensure isolation of energy sources for equipment undergoing maintenance, hot work procedures and permits for work with the potential for generating ignition sources in the presence of flammable or combustible material, and confined space entry permits and procedure to ensure that adequate precautions are in place before entry is allowed into a permit required confined space.

Training:  Sawtooth Caverns has developed and implemented formal operator and maintenance training programs.  Initial training insures that new or reassigned personnel are trained in an overview of the process and operating procedures.  Refresher training is performed at least every three (3) years to ensure

that the operator understands and adheres to the current operating procedures of the process.  Employees are tested to demonstrate their understanding of the training and competency.

Contractors:  Sawtooth Caverns has developed and implemented a program to ensure that contractors used to supplement its workforce to perform maintenance, renovation or specialty work on or near RMP / PSM covered processes are qualified to perform the work and are informed of the potential hazards.  Sawtooth NGL Caverns personnel monitor the contractor activities throughout all maintenance, renovation or specialty work on or new RMP / PSM covered processes.

Pre-startup Safety Reviews (PSSR):  Sawtooth Caverns requires a pre-startup safety review (PSSR) to be performed and documented for any physical modification in the PSM covered processes.  Additionally, any new units added at Sawtooth Caverns which is considered PSM covered processes will also require a PSSR to be performed and documented.

Mechanical Integrity:   Sawtooth Caverns has developed and implemented procedures to maintain the on-going mechanical integrity of critical process equipment in accordance with National Fire Protection Association NFPA-58 Liquefied Petroleum Gas Code requirements for LP-Gas Storage and industry recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices.
Inspections and tests are documented and deficiencies outside of the acceptable limits are corrected before further use or in a safe and timely manner.  

Hot Work Permits:  Sawtooth Caverns has developed and implemented a hot work permit system in accordance with the OSHA 29 CFR Part 1910 requirements for hot work operations conducted on or near a covered process.

Management of Change:  Sawtooth Caverns requires that a management of change (MOC) be performed for any modification to equipment, procedures, products and process parameters of a PSM covered process.  

Incident Investigation:  Sawtooth Caverns requires that any incidents that resu

lted in the release of regulated substances, or a near miss, must be investigated as soon as possible, but no later than 48 hours following the incident.  Sawtooth Caverns has established a system to promptly address and resolve incident investigation findings and recommendations.  

Compliance Audits:  Sawtooth Caverns conducts audits on a regular basis to ensure that the facility is in compliance with applicable all the elements of the EPA 40 CFR Part 68 Accidental Release Prevention Requirements, Program 3 Risk Management Plan (RMP), all the elements of OSHA 29 CFR Part 1910.119 Process Safety Management (PSM) of Highly Hazardous Chemicals regulation, and the requirements of the National Fire Protection Association NFPA-58 Liquefied Petroleum Gas Code requirements for LP-Gas Storage and all applicable codes and regulations.

Five-year Accident History:
4/1/2025: 
The Sawtooth Caverns facility experienced an operational incident that resulted in the unplanned release of approximately 15,000 pounds of liquefied butane. The release was promptly detected, and facility personnel immediately initiated established emergency response procedures in accordance with company policy. Local emergency services  including the Millard County Sheriffs Department, Delta Fire Department, and Millard County EMS  were notified without delay and responded to the scene.
The incident was swiftly brought under control; however, one employee sustained a severe injury to their left arm, necessitating surgical intervention. A comprehensive incident investigation was conducted to determine root causes, and corrective actions have since been implemented to enhance safety protocols and prevent future occurrences.

Emergency Response Program Information:
Sawtooth Caverns Emergency Response Plan is site-specific.  It includes required actions by plant employees as well as required notification and coordination with local responders and agencies. All employees are trained in the execution of th

e Emergency Response Plan and drills are conducted.

Trade Secrets:  There are no trade secrets applicable to Sawtooth Caverns processes.

Planned Changes to Improve Safety:  Sawtooth Caverns has recently established a Safety Council composed of representatives from multiple departments. This council meets regularly to review safety performance, address employee concerns, and recommend enhancements to procedures and training. In addition, the facility has scheduled equipment upgrades, including replacement of select piping and manifold systems with materials specifically engineered for improved performance and durability under high-pressure operating conditions.
